headline: High-risk data and action mismatch: Plane can ingest files and call external APIs while the other agent is a non-runnable docs-only list with no execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot ingest B's outputs directly. B can handle files and external APIs, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. Any prompt-injection pathway would require unusual manual copy-paste or an external workflow not shown here.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A's downstream workflow, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting B outputs into any instruction-following system.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. B can upload file contents and call external APIs, but there is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class flowing from A to B. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of files into B.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files into B's upload surface, B can transmit them externally.
IF A is extended to produce files or secrets, those could be forwarded into B.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive files to B unless necessary.
Use a separate redacted workspace for B.
Review B's outbound API destinations before use.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on file uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, while B explicitly lacks filesystem write and only has broad network egress. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited to external API contention, which is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator assigns them the same mutable OAuth scope, overlap appears.
mitigations: Keep B read-only with respect to shared storage.
Do not grant A new write or network permissions without coordination.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a docs-only list and cannot generate operational facts or actions, so B cannot reliably treat A as an authoritative upstream agent. B does have downstream action surfaces via APIs and file uploads, but the pairwise cascade is weak because A produces no executable output and no direct handoff is documented.
conditions: IF A is replaced with a runnable agent that emits task instructions, B could act on them.
IF an operator manually converts A's content into tasks for B, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not use A as an authoritative source for task creation.
Require human review before B acts on any imported content.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before API actions.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source, non-runnable repository listing with no touched data classes, so it presents no direct residency or retention issue. B handles files, notes, issues, and external APIs, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes or a cross-border policy mismatch. The compliance concern is therefore limited and undocumented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into B, residency and retention review is required.
IF B's external APIs store uploaded files outside the operator's jurisdiction, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B.
Review B's retention settings before uploading files.
requires-engineering: document data-processing terms for external APIs.
